title: Gameworld Parameter Set
description: The set of all map and world parameters of a foundation, grouped by region generation stage. A parameter that is left out keeps its default. Section numbers refer to docs/map-generation.md, and those marked society to docs/society-generation.md.

$schema.description: The address of this schema, so an editor can show help for the file. Ignored when the file is loaded.

Siting.description: Sited stage: the three levels of cells, the ocean seeds and the elevation types (§3, §4, §5.1, §8).

RegionGridSizeKm.description: Grid spacing of the region level in km: the size of a region (§4).

RegionJitter.description: How far a region site may lie from the centre of its grid square: 0 gives a square grid, 1 lets the site be anywhere in its square (§3.1).

ZoneGridSizeKm.description: Grid spacing of the zone level in km. The sizes are kept nested: it is clamped to between 1/16 and 1/1.5 of the region size (§4).

ZoneJitter.description: How far a zone site may lie from the centre of its grid square: 0 gives a square grid, 1 lets the site be anywhere in its square (§3.1).

ZoneWarp.description: Border warp of the zone level, in cell sizes. 0 leaves the borders of zone cells unwarped. It affects which zone cell owns a patch cell (§3.2, §4).

ZoneWarpFrequency.description: Warp noise cycles per zone cell. Only used when ZoneWarp is above 0 (§3.2).

PatchGridSizeKm.description: Grid spacing of the patch level in km. It is clamped to between 1/16 and 1/1.5 of the zone size (§4).

PatchJitter.description: How far a patch site may lie from the centre of its grid square: 0 gives a square grid, 1 lets the site be anywhere in its square (§3.1).

PatchWarp.description: Border warp of the patch level, in cell sizes. Coastlines and zone and region borders run along patch borders, so this gives all of them their wavy shape. 0 gives straight borders (§3.2, §4).

PatchWarpFrequency.description: Warp noise cycles per patch cell: lower gives broader waves in the borders (§3.2).

NestLevels.description: Classify a point through its patch only (point → patch → zone → region), so zone borders, region borders and coastlines all run along patch borders. Only true is supported: every later layer assumes nesting (§4).

OceanSeedsPerRegion.description: How many of the zone cells it owns each region chooses as ocean seeds: a count drawn evenly from Min to Max. More seeds give more sea (§5.1).

ElevationWeights.description: Relative weights of the four land elevation types, drawn per zone cell. Whole numbers; with the defaults 5 of 13 zone cells are Flat Land (§8).

Outline.description: Outlined stage: ocean links, ocean expansion and zone mergers (§5.2, §5.3, §6.1).

OceanLinkChance.description: Chance that an ocean seed makes one link, to its nearest other ocean seed. Tested when the seed does not make two links. Every zone cell under a link becomes ocean (§5.2).

OceanDoubleLinkChance.description: Chance that an ocean seed makes two links, to its two nearest other ocean seeds. Tested first (§5.2).

OceanLinkRangeRegions.description: How many regions away an ocean seed looks for seeds to link to: 2 is a 5 × 5 block of regions. A region can be Outlined when all regions within this range + 5 rings are Sited, so a larger range makes every lookup reach further (§5.2).

OceanExpansionFrom.description: Which ocean zone cells expand in the first pass. Linked: every zone cell on a link, so a lone ocean seed stays a sea of one zone cell. All: every ocean zone cell, lone seeds too (§5.3).

OceanExpansionPasses.description: Number of ocean expansion passes. Each pass after the first expands from the zone cells the previous pass converted. More passes give more sea; 0 turns expansion off (§5.3).

OceanExpansionWeights.description: Relative weights for an expanding zone cell converting 0, 1, 2 or 3 of its nearest land neighbours to ocean: four numbers in that order. A negative weight counts as 0 (§5.3).

ZoneMergersPerRegion.description: How many of the zone cells it owns each region chooses to merge into their nearest neighbour: a count drawn evenly from Min to Max. A merger that finds no neighbour on its side of the coast still counts (§6.1).

MergeAcrossCoast.description: Let a zone cell merge into its nearest neighbour even when one is land and the other ocean. Off by default: only land-land and ocean-ocean mergers are allowed (§6.1).

Detail.description: Detailed stage: patch mergers, rivers and lakes (§6.3, §10, §11).

PatchMergersPerZoneCell.description: How many of the patch cells it owns each zone cell chooses to merge into their nearest neighbour patch cell in the same zone: a count drawn evenly from Min to Max (§6.3).

Rivers.description: Rivers: grown per region with space colonization, from the sea into the land (§10).

AttractorsPerPatchCell.description: Attraction points scattered in every eligible patch cell. More give denser rivers. River sizes are flows divided by this number, so they read as patches drained (§10.1).

StepKm.description: Length of one growth step, which is one river segment, in km (§10).

InfluenceKm.description: An attractor pulls its nearest river node only within this radius, in km. Raised to at least 1.5 × the step. A large radius gives fewer, straighter rivers; a small one many independent branches (§10, §18.2).

KillKm.description: An attractor is reached once a river node is this close, in km. Raised to at least 1.05 × the step (§10).

RandomMotion.description: Weight of a random unit vector added to the direction of every growth step. 0 gives straight runs towards the attractors (§10.3).

Wander.description: How much of a step's random vector is inherited from the parent node, 0 to 1. Higher makes bends persist over several steps instead of wiggling (§10.3).

PerceptionConeDegrees.description: A river node is only pulled by attractors within ± half this angle of its heading, in degrees. It stops branches hooking back; 360 lets nodes see all round (§10.3).

MainStemDominance.description: A node that already has a child only sprouts a side branch if its own pulls are at least this share of the pulls on the stem beyond it. Higher removes more short side twigs; 0 turns it off (§10.5).

PullPower.description: Weight of one pull by its distance d relative to the influence radius. Normal: every pull has equal weight. Squared: (d / influence)², far attractors pull harder. Root: √(d / influence) (§10.3).

Inertia.description: Weight of the node's current heading in the direction of its next step. 0 is no inertia; higher gives straighter rivers (§10.3).

SkipCoastalPatchCells.description: Put no attractors in coastal patch cells. It keeps river mouths apart and gives the rivers a clear run from the coast into the interior (§10.1).

RiverPoorPrecipitationCutoffMm.description: A flat zone whose site gets less precipitation than this, in mm/yr, is river-poor: its patch cells get 0 or 1 attractor instead of the full number, it is drier for the biomes and it holds no lakes. Higher makes more of the flat zones dry plains (§10.1).

Lakes.description: Lakes: placed per region on the rivers (§11).

Frequency.description: Chance that a patch cell with a suitable river node gets a lake (§11).

MinSizeKm.description: Smallest lake in km, measured as the diameter of a circle of equal area (§11).

MaxSizeKm.description: Largest lake in km, measured as the diameter of a circle of equal area. Sizes are skewed towards small lakes (§11).

Elevation.description: Elevated stage: the height map and the biomes (§12, §13).

HeightMap.description: The height map: a raster per region, fitted to the rivers and the coast (§12).

ChannelSlope.description: River gradient at a flow of 1, in m/m. Higher gives steeper rivers, and with them higher land, since the land rises from the river beds (§12.2).

Concavity.description: Rivers flatten downstream as flow to the power −concavity: higher gives flatter large rivers. The default is 7/16; multiples of 1/16 are computed exactly (§12.2).

HillslopeMultiplier.description: Scales the hillslope of every elevation type (§12).

LevelFlatZones.description: How strongly zones with a river gradient factor below 1 (flat zones by default) are levelled towards the height of their lowest river entry, so they read as a plain at roughly one level. 0 turns levelling off (§12.2).

MountainBelts.description: Strength of the region-scale relief field, which makes groups of neighbouring zones rugged or gentle together. 0 turns it off (§12.1).

RegionRidgeM.description: Ridge height along region borders, in metres. Region borders are watersheds (§12.5).

BasinDivideM.description: Ridge height between two river systems, in metres (§12.5).

DetailNoise.description: Multiplier on the surface detail noise. 0 gives a smooth surface (§12.5).

ChannelDepthM.description: How deep rivers are cut below their bed profile, in metres (§12.6).

SeaDepthM.description: Sea depth 40 km or more from the coast, in metres (§12.5).

Hillslope.description: How steeply the land rises away from rivers and the coast, in m/m, per elevation type. This is what makes the land between the rivers a plain or a range (§12).

RiverGradientFactor.description: Multiplier on the river gradient, per elevation type. A type with a factor below 1 is levelled, see LevelFlatZones (§12.2).

Floodplain.description: Floodplain half-width as a function of the river bed height (§12).

Points.description: Control points of a monotone spline from river bed height to floodplain half-width. The half-width is constant beyond the end points and never less than 0.75 × the raster cell size (§12).

items.description: One control point: the floodplain half-width at a river bed height.

HalfWidthM.description: Floodplain half-width in metres at that bed height.

ScaleWithRiverSize.description: When on, the points give the half-width at a flow of 100 and other flows get × √(flow / 100), so big rivers get wide floodplains (§12).

Biomes.description: Biomes: one per land patch, from temperature and aridity (§13).

Cooling.description: Control points of a monotone spline from height to the cooling of the Initial Temperature. Constant below the first point; above the last it continues along the last segment's slope. The defaults are much steeper than the real atmosphere, so land below 1000 m still gets cold highlands (§13.1).

items.description: One control point: the cooling at a height.

RiverPoorPrecipitationFactor.description: The precipitation of a patch in a river-poor flat zone is multiplied by this for the biomes. Lower makes the dry plains drier (§13.1).

MangroveMinTemperatureC.description: A coastal patch in a flat or lowland zone becomes Mangrove when it is at least this warm, in °C, and at least as wet as MangroveMinAridity (§13.2).

MangroveMinAridity.description: The smallest aridity (precipitation ÷ the dryness threshold of the temperature) at which a warm low coast becomes Mangrove. Below 0.5 is desert, 0.5 to 1 steppe, above 1 humid (§13.2).

Planning.description: Planned stage: Prospects for cities and towns, which of them are on show (§15), and the potential population (society §3). The Settled stage has no parameters of its own: the travel network connects the Prospects on show (§16).

ProspectsPerRegion.description: Prospects per region. Regions with little habitable land end up with fewer (§15.5).

CityProspectsPerRegion.description: How many of a region's Prospects are for cities, at most. The rest are for towns (§15.5).

SpacingKm.description: Smallest distance between two Prospects, in km. Prospects for cities keep 2.5 × this from each other. When a region cannot fit its Prospects the spacing is relaxed by 15 % at a time, down to one patch size (§15.5).

Weights.description: Weights of the five factors in the score of a patch. Only their proportions matter. A negative weight counts as 0; if all are 0 the plain mean is used (§15.4).

Resources.description: Weight of the resources factor: food, fresh water, building materials and fuel, fish and trade goods on and around the patch (§15.3).

Geography.description: Weight of the geography factor: buildable ground, waterside and defence (§15.3).

Trade.description: Weight of the trade factor: gateways (river mouths, harbours, heads of navigation, confluences) and how much of the region's food is within reach (§15.3).

Climate.description: Weight of the climate factor: a comfortable temperature and enough moisture (§15.3).

Prosperity.description: Weight of the prosperity factor: the Prosperity field at the spot (§15.3).

OneOnShowScoreSum.description: The sum of the scores of a region's Prospects at or below which only 1 of them is on show. The number on show grows evenly with the sum from here to AllOnShowScoreSum. Prospects on show are drawn on a map and connected by roads, river routes and sea lanes. With the defaults about 1 region in 20 shows a single Prospect and the median region shows 13 of its 20 (§15.6, §16).

AllOnShowScoreSum.description: The sum of the scores of a region's Prospects at or above which all of them are on show. With the defaults about 1 region in 10 shows all 20 (§15.6).

RichScore.description: A Prospect with at least this score (0 to 100) is Rich: a map draws it in gold. With the defaults about a quarter of the Prospects on show are Rich (§15.6, §17).

PoorScore.description: A Prospect with a score (0 to 100) below this is Poor: a map draws it in bronze. The ones between are Average, in silver. With the defaults about a fifth of the Prospects on show are Poor (§15.6, §17).

Population.description: The potential population of a region: how many persons its land can feed. The races that are on share it (society §3).

PersonsPerKm2.description: Persons per km² on land with a food supply of 1 at a middling Prosperity. The potential population of a patch is its area × this × its food supply × its Prosperity factor (society §3.1).

ProsperityEffect.description: How much the Prosperity field moves the potential population of a patch: the factor runs from 1 − this at the lowest Prosperity to 1 + this at the highest. 0 turns the effect of Prosperity off (society §3.1).

RacesPerRegion.description: The most races a region holds: its main races and its minority races. Only they share the potential population of the region. A number at or above the number of races that are on, with no minority races, gives every race its plain share (society §3.3).

MinorityRacesPerRegion.description: How many of the races of a region are minority races: the last places, which go to the race whose turn it is in the region. The other places go to the main races, the largest by their plain shares. Every race that is on has one turn per place in every 6 × 5 block of regions with the default 28 races (society §3.3).

RacesPerCity.description: The most races a city holds. They are races of its region: the largest around the Prospect, and a last one drawn with the minority races weighted up (society §5.1).

RacesPerTown.description: The most races a town holds. They are races of its region: the largest around the Prospect, and a last one drawn with the minority races weighted up (society §5.1).

MinorityMinPersons.description: How many persons of a race the land of a region must feed by the plain shares for the race to take a minority place there (society §3.3).

MinorityShare.description: The share of the potential population of a region that a minority race is lifted towards, 0 to 0.9. A minority race that already holds more keeps its share, and one that lives on a few patches only stays below it. 0 turns the lift off (society §3.4).

MinorityBoost.description: The factor on a minority race of the region in the draw for the last race of a city or a town. 1 gives it no advantage (society §5.1).

HinterlandShare.description: How much of the potential population of the whole region a city or a town draws on, beside the patch of its Prospect and the land patches around it, 0 to 1. It lets a race of the region that does not live nearby into the city or town (society §5.1).

Fields.description: The four Fields: noise maps that drive climate, biomes and resources. They have no stage (§9).

Precipitation.description: Precipitation in mm/yr, on a logarithmic scale. Its Distribution spreads the moisture classes of the biomes evenly: the points lie near the bounds between desert, steppe, sub-humid, humid and wet. Warped into belts. Feeds the biomes and thins the rivers of dry flat zones (§9, §13.2).

FeatureSizeKm.description: Size of the features of the noise in km: larger gives slower changes across the map.

Octaves.description: Number of noise octaves: a whole number, at least 1. More octaves add finer detail.

Lacunarity.description: Frequency multiplier from one octave to the next.

Gain.description: Amplitude multiplier from one octave to the next: lower makes the finer octaves weaker.

Min.description: The value at the strongest lows of the noise. At least 1 for the logarithmic Precipitation field.

Max.description: The value at the strongest highs of the noise. Only the strongest highs and lows reach Min and Max.

WarpKm.description: Strength of the warp in km: about the furthest the position the field is read at is moved. A warp of a few feature sizes draws the round features of the noise out into winding belts. 0 turns the warp off.

WarpFeatureSizeKm.description: Size of the features of the warp noise in km: larger gives longer, straighter belts. Only used when WarpKm is above 0.

Distribution.description: How the values are spread over the map: each point gives the share of the map that lies below a value. Min is the point at share 0 and Max the point at share 1, and a monotone spline runs through the points (through the logarithm of the values for Precipitation). The shares hold over a large area; a single view of the map can differ. Empty gives the bell shape of the noise: half the map lies in the middle quarter of the range between Min and Max (§9).

items.description: One point of the distribution of a field: the share of the map that lies below a value.

Share.description: Share of the map that lies below the value: above 0 and below 1. A point outside that is ignored.

Value.description: The value, in the unit of the field. Between Min and Max, and the values rise with the shares.

InitialTemperature.description: Initial Temperature in °C at sea level, on a linear scale, warped into belts. It is cooled by the height of the patch for the biomes. Its Distribution has one point at each bound between two thermal belts, so the shares are the shares of the belts at sea level (§9, §13.1, §13.2).

Bedrocks.description: The bedrock types and their relative weight under each elevation type. The bedrock of a zone is drawn by these weights (§14.1). The resource rules know the nine ids of the defaults; a bedrock with another id gives no bedrock-bound resources.

items.description: A bedrock type and its weight under each elevation type.

Id.description: The id the resource rules know the bedrock by: shield, foldBelt, granite, volcanic, basalt, ophiolite, carbonate, clastic or alluvium.

Name.description: The name shown for the bedrock.

Weights.description: Relative weight of the bedrock under each elevation type. Whole numbers; 0 means never under that type.

Races.description: The races: the peoples that can live in the world. Add a race by adding an entry, and switch a race on or off with Enabled. The potential population of a region is shared between the races that are on, by their frequency in the biome of each patch and their height modifier at its height (society §2 and §3.2). A file that gives this list replaces the whole default list.

items.description: A race: a people that can live in the world, and how frequent it is in each biome and at each height.

Id.description: The id the generated data knows the race by. Unique in the list; keep it when the name changes.

Name.description: The name shown for the race.

Enabled.description: Whether the race lives in the world. A race that is off gets no population, and the races that are on share the land without it.

BiomeFrequency.description: How frequent the race is in each biome, relative to the other races. The potential population of a patch is shared between the races that are on in proportion to these numbers, so only the proportions between the races within one biome matter. List only the biomes the race lives in: a biome that is left out has the frequency 0, and a frequency of 0 is not written to the file. A negative number counts as 0 (society §3.2).

TemperateMixedForest.description: Value for Temperate mixed forest patches.

TemperateBroadleafForest.description: Value for Temperate broadleaf forest patches.

TemperateRainForest.description: Value for Temperate rain forest patches.

TropicalDryForest.description: Value for Tropical dry forest patches.

TropicalRainForest.description: Value for Tropical rain forest patches.

HeightModifier.description: How the height of the land changes the frequency of the race: control points from the mean height of a patch to a factor on its biome frequencies. The factor runs in a straight line between two points and is constant beyond the first and the last. Two points at the same height make a step: the first holds below that height, the second from that height and up. So [200 → 0, 200 → 1] is a race that only lives from 200 m and up, and [200 → 1, 200 → 0] one that only lives below 200 m. Left out, the height does not matter to the race (society §3.2).

items.description: One control point of the height modifier of a race: the factor at a height.

HeightM.description: Height in metres above sea level.

Factor.description: What the biome frequencies of the race are multiplied by at that height. 0 means the race does not live at that height; a negative number counts as 0.
